evals.prompt: We want agents that read supplier emails, extract order changes and update our ERP. A colleague proposes a classifier agent, an extraction agent and an ERP agent. Is that the right architecture?
evals.expected_output: Start from a workflow or single-agent baseline; the classifier is a router step; ERP writes run in code after approval.
expectations: Recommends starting from a baseline (workflow in code or a single agent) and measuring it on real tasks
Treats classification as a router or workflow step unless it makes a runtime decision
The ERP update runs in deterministic code or behind approval, not as an agent's free action
Asks for or proposes caps and a defined outcome at each cap
Does not endorse three agents without an eval result that justifies them

evals.prompt: Our research agent's context blows up because search returns 40 full documents per call. Should we split it into several specialist agents?
evals.expected_output: Fix context first: trim or offload results; then a read-only subagent with a short report; specialists last.
expectations: First trims or offloads the tool results (or bounds them on the server)
Then suggests moving the noisy read-only part into a subagent that returns a short report
Does not recommend splitting by role as the first step

evals.prompt: Review this proposal: a planner agent passes a summary to a coder agent, which passes one to a tester agent, which passes one to a reviewer agent; the loop runs until the reviewer approves.
evals.expected_output: Split by context, not role; pass reports on unchanged; the loop needs a cap and a deterministic check.
expectations: Names the role chain as costly coordination (split by context, not by role)
Flags the summaries passed between agents (telephone game) and recommends structured reports passed on unchanged
Flags the uncapped loop and asks what happens at the cap
Prefers a deterministic check (tests) over an LLM reviewer as the loop's exit

evals.prompt: Classifying invoices into 5 cost centres must be very reliable. Should two agents debate the answer?
evals.expected_output: Parallel samples with a majority vote, or a deterministic check, rather than debate.
expectations: Recommends parallel samples and a majority vote instead of debate
Mentions measuring against real labelled invoices

evals.prompt: Write down the architecture decision for our ticket-triage graph: triage and review agents in an evaluator-optimizer loop, max 2 rounds, MCP tools, results reviewed by a person before they're saved.
evals.expected_output: A decision record in the DECISION-RECORD.md format.
expectations: States the baseline and its eval score (or marks it as missing)
Has one row per decision from DECISION-RECORD.md (coordination, task assignment, ..., side effects)
Failure handling names the 2-round cap and what happens at it
Side effects say the person approves and code saves
